experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Experience a centuries-old Hungarian bathing culture with indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs.

experiences.name: Old Town Prague Walking History Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the famous Astronomical Clock chime, explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov), and discover Gothic, Baroque, and Art Nouveau architecture spanning over 1,000 years of history.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Hungarian National History Walk
experiences.description: Climb or take the historic funicular up to Buda Castle, explore the Hungarian National Gallery, stroll through the cobblestone streets of the Castle District, and visit Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion for breathtaking views over the Danube.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube at sunset and after dark to witness Budapest's illuminated Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage panorama. Includes light commentary on the city's rich Austro-Hungarian history.
experiences.location: Vigadó Square Pier, Pest Riverbank, Budapest

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) or night bus to the city center (~60 CZK). Check in to your accommodation, drop off luggage, and grab a late-night snack near the hostel/hotel area. Get a good night's rest to prepare for full days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night kebab or convenience store snack near your accommodation (~100–150 CZK / ~€4–6).

day_by_day.notes: Keep your airport transfer simple and cheap. The AE bus runs to Masarykovo nádraží in ~35 min. Have Czech Koruna (CZK) ready or use a card. Exchange only a small amount at the airport if needed — rates are better in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague adventure with a visit to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore the castle grounds for free (interior buildings have a paid ticket, ~250 CZK for the basic circuit). Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through Malá Strana (Lesser Town), crossing the iconic Charles Bridge lined with baroque statues. Stroll through the Old Town (Staré Město), visit the Old Town Square, and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour — completely free. Browse the narrow medieval streets and soak in the Gothic and Baroque architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Wenceslas Square for an evening walk through the heart of modern Prague. Enjoy dinner at a traditional Czech pub (pivnice) in the Old Town area.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (koláč) and coffee at a local bakery near your accommodation (~80–120 CZK / ~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Trdelník (chimney cake) as a street snack, plus a cheap sandwich from a local deli (~100–150 CZK / ~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech pub meal — svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings and a half-liter of Czech beer at a local pivnice (~200–300 CZK / ~€8–12).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague is very hilly around the castle area. The Charles Bridge is most magical early morning or evening when crowds thin. Public transport day pass (~120 CZK) is excellent value if you want to skip some walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Explore the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and the surrounding synagogues (combined ticket ~500 CZK, or admire the exterior for free). Walk along the Vltava riverbank for beautiful views of the city skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood — two authentic, less-touristy districts beloved by locals. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (exterior is free; observation deck ~250 CZK if budget allows) with its famous crawling baby sculptures. Browse local markets and independent coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a classical music concert — Prague has many budget-friendly evening concerts in historic churches (tickets from ~300–500 CZK / ~€12–20). Alternatively, enjoy a beer at a rooftop bar or a local craft beer pub in Žižkov, known as Prague's pub district.

meals.breakfast: Hostel/hotel breakfast if included, or a local café with eggs and coffee (~120–150 CZK / ~€5–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Czech canteen (jídelna) — these worker-style cafeterias offer huge, authentic meals for ~100–180 CZK / ~€4–7.
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget Italian restaurant in Vinohrady (~200–250 CZK / ~€8–10), or grab street food at a local market stall.

day_by_day.notes: Žižkov has an edgy, bohemian vibe and is far cheaper than the tourist center. The Žižkov TV Tower is one of Prague's most unusual landmarks — worth seeing even from outside. September evenings can be cool; bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — visit Letná Park (Letenské sady) for incredible free panoramic views over Prague and the Vltava River. Locals jog and cycle here. There's a famous beer garden (Letenský zámeček) if you fancy an early afternoon drink with a view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nové Město (New Town) and visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — tickets ~200 CZK / ~€8, with impressive historical and natural history collections. Then prepare for your evening journey to Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Board an overnight train or budget bus from Prague to Budapest. RegioJet and FlixBus offer affordable routes (~€15–30 one way). Overnight travel saves on accommodation costs. Arrive in Budapest early the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a croissant at a café near your accommodation (~100 CZK / ~€4).
meals.lunch: Hearty lunch at a Czech canteen to fuel up before travel (~150–200 CZK / ~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Pack snacks and sandwiches for the overnight bus/train journey to save money (~100 CZK / ~€4 at a supermarket like Albert or Billa).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport in advance for the best budget prices. RegioJet buses are comfortable with free Wi-Fi and entertainment screens. Keep your valuables secure on overnight transport. The journey is approximately 6–7 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Budapest early morning. Check in to your accommodation or store luggage if room isn't ready. Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most beautiful indoor market. Browse stalls selling Hungarian paprika, salami, lángos (fried dough), and folk crafts. Great for a cheap, authentic breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the iconic Liberty Bridge to Buda side and hike up Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) — completely free! The Citadella fortress at the top offers breathtaking 360° panoramic views of Budapest, the Danube, and both the Buda and Pest sides of the city. A must-do on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Danube Promenade on the Pest side as the sun sets and the city lights up. The Chain Bridge and Buda Castle illuminated at night is one of Europe's most spectacular urban views. Grab dinner in the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's vibrant nightlife hub.

meals.breakfast: Lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) at the Great Market Hall (~800–1200 HUF / ~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Goulash soup (gulyásleves) and fresh bread at a local étterem (restaurant) near the market (~2000–3000 HUF / ~€5–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a ruin bar or casual restaurant in the Jewish Quarter — try chicken paprikash or stuffed cabbage (~3000–4500 HUF / ~€8–12).

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forints (HUF). Avoid currency exchange booths at tourist spots — use ATMs or exchange offices in the city center. September is a wonderful time to visit Budapest — warm days, mild evenings, and fewer crowds than summer peak.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) and the Castle District — walk up via the funicular (Sikló) for ~1400 HUF one way, or hike up for free. Explore Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) exterior and the stunning Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — the terraces offer fairy-tale views over the Danube and the Hungarian Parliament. Basic access is free; upper terraces ~1000 HUF.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back to Pest and explore the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) from the outside — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings, best viewed from the Danube bank. Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and City Park (Városliget) — both completely free. The park has a lake, a replica castle (Vajdahunyad), and plenty of space to relax.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar scene — start at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar in the Jewish Quarter. These eclectic bars are set in abandoned buildings decorated with vintage furniture and art. Very budget-friendly with cheap local beer and cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee at a local pékség (bakery) in the Castle District (~800–1200 HUF / ~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Kürtőskalács (chimney cake) as a street snack, plus a hearty bowl of bean soup at a local spot in City Park (~1500–2500 HUF / ~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Affordable dinner at a local étterem in the Jewish Quarter — pörkölt (meat stew) with nokedli dumplings (~2500–3500 HUF / ~€6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to visit Szimpla Kert as they host a farmers' market in the morning. The ruin bars are cultural institutions, not just party venues — even non-drinkers enjoy the unique atmosphere. Wear comfortable shoes for the Buda Castle hike.

day_by_day.morning: Visit one of Budapest's legendary thermal baths — a quintessential Hungarian experience. The Rudas Baths are more budget-friendly (~5000–6000 HUF / ~€13–16) and less touristy than Széchenyi. Alternatively, Széchenyi Baths in City Park are the most famous (~6500–8000 HUF / ~€17–21). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in mineral-rich thermal pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Dohány Street Synagogue (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and a stunning piece of Moorish Revival architecture. Entrance ~5000 HUF / ~€13. Walk through the Jewish Quarter's memorial park and Holocaust memorial. Then browse the eclectic antique shops and vintage stores along Király utca.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget Danube evening stroll along the Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a poignant and moving Holocaust memorial that is free to visit. Watch the Parliament building light up across the river. End the evening with a farewell Hungarian dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Hungarian breakfast at your accommodation or a local café — eggs, cold cuts, bread, and coffee (~1500–2000 HUF / ~€4–5).
meals.lunch: Quick and cheap lunch at a local falafel or gyros spot in the Jewish Quarter (~1500–2000 HUF / ~€4–5).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — try a traditional Hungarian restaurant for töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage) or halászlé (fisherman's soup) with wine (~4000–6000 HUF / ~€10–15).

day_by_day.notes: Book thermal baths in advance online to secure a time slot and sometimes get a small discount. The Shoes on the Danube memorial is especially powerful at night when illuminated. September evenings by the Danube can be breezy — bring a layer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) for an overview of Hungary's fascinating history from prehistoric times to the 20th century (~2000 HUF / ~€5). Alternatively, take a relaxed walk through the Inner City (Belváros) and browse local souvenir shops for paprika, Tokaji wine, and Herend porcelain gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a local café for a final Hungarian coffee and pastry (rétes/strudel). Pack up, check out of accommodation, and make your way to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or your onward transport hub. The 100E airport bus runs directly from Deák Ferenc tér (~1000 HUF / ~€2.5) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer option.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels home with wonderful memories of Prague and Budapest!

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — lángos or pastry with coffee at a local café (~1000–1500 HUF / ~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite near your accommodation before departure (~2000–3000 HUF / ~€5–8).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on your return flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The 100E airport bus is significantly cheaper than taxis or rideshares. Use any remaining HUF at the airport — coins cannot be exchanged back. Keep all receipts if you plan to claim VAT refunds on purchases over €175.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit (Flight UA arriving at 22:30)
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or an Uber/taxi to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at the hotel or a nearby 24-hour convenience store (e.g., a local bakery or Potrefená Husa if open late near your area)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely an arrival day. No activities are scheduled before landing. Keep your first night light — hydrate, rest, and prepare for a full day in Prague tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast, then head to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and cross the iconic Charles Bridge, admiring its Baroque statues. Continue into the Old Town (Staré Město) and visit the Old Town Square, the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), and the Church of Our Lady before Týn. Browse the surrounding streets and local souvenir shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing evening stroll along the Vltava River embankment. Watch the sunset over Charles Bridge from a riverside viewpoint. Head to a traditional Czech restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — try Café Louvre or a nearby bakery for pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch near Old Town Square — try Lokál Dlouhááá (mid-range, authentic Czech cuisine: svíčková, goulash, fresh Pilsner Urquell)
meals.dinner: U Fleků Brewery Restaurant — a historic Prague brewpub serving traditional Czech dishes like roast pork knee and house-brewed dark lager (mid-range, ~€15–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a very walkable day covering ~6–8 km. Prague Castle opens at 9:00 AM. Consider buying a combined ticket for the castle complex (~€15–20). The Astronomical Clock performs on the hour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Explore the Jewish Museum complex, which includes six synagogues (Spanish, Pinkas, Maisel, Old-New, Klaus, and Ceremonial Hall) and the hauntingly beautiful Old Jewish Cemetery — one of the oldest in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) — the heart of modern Prague and a hub of Czech history (site of the 1968 Prague Spring and 1989 Velvet Revolution). Visit the National Museum at the top of the square. Afterward, explore Vinohrady neighborhood for a taste of local Prague life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is renowned for its live classical performances. Check listings at the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or Rudolfinum concert hall for evening performances. Afterward, enjoy a nightcap at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial — a stunning Art Nouveau café serving a full Czech breakfast (mid-range, ~€10–15)
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (container food market near Vinohrady) — great street food variety, budget-friendly (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Eska — a modern Czech bistro with farm-to-table dishes and freshly baked bread (mid-range, ~€20–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Jewish Museum tickets online in advance (~€15–20). Classical concert tickets range from €15–40 depending on the venue and program. September is an excellent month for Prague's cultural calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration of Vyšehrad — a lesser-visited historic fortress overlooking the Vltava River. Walk the ramparts, visit the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, and stroll through the Vyšehrad Cemetery where famous Czechs like Dvořák and Mucha are buried. Peaceful and far fewer tourists than the castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Mucha Museum (dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha) or the National Gallery's trade fair palace (Veletržní Palác) for modern and contemporary Czech art. Spend time exploring Nové Město (New Town) and the Palác Akropolis area.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Prague — explore the vibrant Žižkov or Vinohrady neighborhoods for local bars and restaurants. This is your last night in Prague before heading to Budapest tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Vyšehrad — grab supplies from a local deli or Naše Maso butcher shop (excellent Czech charcuterie and sandwiches, ~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Kantýna — a stylish Czech restaurant in Nové Město known for quality meat dishes and local craft beers (mid-range, ~€18–28/person)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is free to enter (individual attractions have small fees). Pack a light jacket — September evenings in Prague can be cool (~14–18°C). Begin packing tonight for the morning transfer to Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Prague accommodation. Take a scenic train journey from Praha Hlavní Nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti Station — approximately 6.5–7 hours by RegioJet or EC train. Enjoy the Central European countryside as you travel. Trains depart around 7:00–9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to your Budapest accommodation. Once settled, take a walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side for stunning views of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Parliament. Get your bearings in this grand city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — even if it's closing, the exterior is impressive. Then head to the Jewish Quarter (District VII) and the famous ruin bars area around Kazinczy Street for a vibrant Friday/Saturday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Prague Main Station before boarding
meals.lunch: On the train — pack snacks or purchase from the dining car (RegioJet has a good onboard café, ~€5–10)
meals.dinner: Kőleves (Stone Soup) in the Jewish Quarter — a cozy, mid-range Hungarian restaurant with excellent goulash and Jewish-Hungarian fusion dishes (~€15–22/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance on RegioJet.com or Rail Europe (~€25–45 one way). The Prague–Budapest train is one of the most scenic rail journeys in Central Europe. Arrive at Prague station 30 minutes early. Saturday evenings in Budapest's ruin bar district are lively — great for atmosphere even if just walking through.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) to the Buda side and hike or take the funicular up to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota). Explore the Hungarian National Gallery inside the castle and enjoy panoramic views over Pest. Walk through the Castle District's cobblestone streets and visit Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Buda and visit the historic Gellért Hill — hike up (or take a bus) to the Citadella for sweeping 360° views of Budapest. Afterward, visit the famous Gellért Thermal Baths — one of Budapest's most beautiful Art Nouveau spas — for a relaxing afternoon soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pest via the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd). Stroll along Váci Street (main pedestrian shopping street) and enjoy the illuminated Parliament Building from the Danube embankment at night — one of Europe's most spectacular urban views.

meals.breakfast: Centrál Kávéház — a grand historic Budapest café serving Hungarian breakfast (eggs, cold cuts, pastries) in an elegant setting (~€10–14)
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant near Fisherman's Bastion — mid-range Hungarian cuisine with incredible views (~€15–22/person)
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant in the city center offering modern Hungarian cuisine paired with excellent local wines (~€25–35/person)

day_by_day.notes: Gellért Thermal Baths entry is ~€25–30 (book online in advance on weekends). Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops. The baths are open until 8:00 PM. The Parliament building exterior is best viewed after dark when lit up — absolutely stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~€20). Afterward, explore Kossuth Square and the nearby Ethnographic Museum. Head to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and Millennium Monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in City Park (Városliget) — visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (the largest in Budapest, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque building) for a midday soak. Alternatively, visit Vajdahunyad Castle within the park. Explore the Museum of Fine Arts on the edge of Heroes' Square.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter more deeply — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai Zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe. Browse the quirky ruin bars (Szimpla Kert is a must-see). End the night with a Danube river cruise for a magical illuminated view of both banks.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — an opulent historic café often called 'the most beautiful café in the world.' Splurge on a Hungarian breakfast here (~€15–20, worth it for the experience)
meals.lunch: Széchenyi Baths area — grab a light lunch at the park kiosk or a nearby café (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Mazel Tov — a stunning ruin-bar-style restaurant in the Jewish Quarter serving Middle Eastern-Hungarian fusion in a gorgeous courtyard setting (~€18–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at jegy.parlament.hu. Széchenyi Baths entry is ~€25–30. The Great Synagogue is open Monday–Friday and Sunday (~€15 entry). Danube river cruises run ~€15–25 (1–2 hours); book at the dock or online.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Hungarian history. Alternatively, explore the charming Király Street and Gozsdu Courtyard for local boutiques and morning coffee culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration: visit the Central Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — browse stalls selling Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, handmade crafts, and chimney cakes (kürtőskalács). Pick up souvenirs and local food items. Enjoy a final walk across the Chain Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest before heading to the airport or your next destination. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent cities.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — a legendary Budapest patisserie and café, perfect for a final Hungarian breakfast with pastries and coffee (~€12–16)
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall food stalls — try lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese), kürtőskalács, and Hungarian sausages (~€6–10)
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — a sophisticated yet accessible modern Hungarian restaurant for a memorable farewell meal (~€30–45/person, splurge-worthy for the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics — Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport is ~30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or the 100E airport bus (~€3). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. The Great Market Hall closes early on Sundays and is closed Mondays — plan accordingly. Pack paprika and Tokaji wine as the best Hungarian souvenirs!

day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes-Benz S-Class or similar) whisks you to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of Champagne at the hotel bar before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night light supper at the hotel's 24-hour lounge or room service – charcuterie board, smoked salmon, and a glass of premium Czech wine to wind down after travel.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Keep Day 1 light – rest is priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish hotel breakfast. At 10:00, embark on a private guided walking tour of Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the iconic Old Town Square, marvel at the medieval Astronomical Clock (Orloj), and stroll through the charming baroque and gothic streets with your expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge adorned with baroque statues, then ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Enjoy a private tour of St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Panoramic views of the red-roofed city from the castle ramparts are unmissable.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Vltava River. Followed by a private candlelit dinner at a Michelin-recognized fine dining restaurant in Malá Strana (Lesser Town), such as Field or La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, featuring modern Czech tasting menus with wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel – eggs benedict, smoked trout, fresh pastries, artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana – Neo-Renaissance interiors, Czech classics elevated with French technique (svíčková, duck confit, premium desserts).
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – 11-course degustation of reimagined Czech heritage cuisine with sommelier-curated wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Prague Castle private tour to skip public queues. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Sunset typically around 19:30 in mid-September – time rooftop cocktails accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – one of the best-preserved Jewish quarters in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), the Spanish Synagogue, and the Maisel Synagogue. Your guide will bring centuries of rich and poignant history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods – Prague's bohemian art districts. Visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, then browse high-end Czech design boutiques and galleries along Náměstí Míru. Optional: private visit to the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive evening at the Prague State Opera or the Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni in 1787) – attend a world-class opera, ballet, or classical concert performance. Pre-arrange premium box seats. Post-performance dinner at Alcron Restaurant at the Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel – Prague's iconic fine dining institution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – seasonal fruit, yogurt parfait, freshly baked croissants, eggs to order, premium Arabica coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Eska – modern Czech cuisine in a beautifully restored industrial space; sourdough bread, fermented vegetables, grass-fed meats.
meals.dinner: Post-opera dinner at Alcron Restaurant – celebrated seafood and contemporary European cuisine; signature lobster bisque and pan-seared sea bass with Czech Riesling.

day_by_day.notes: Book opera/concert tickets well in advance – September is peak cultural season in Prague. The Estates Theatre is a UNESCO-recognized landmark in itself. Dress code: smart formal for the opera.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure – optional spa treatment at the hotel's wellness center or a sunrise private photography walk along the Vltava River embankment. At 10:30, depart on a private half-day excursion to Karlštejn Castle (30 km from Prague) – a stunning 14th-century Gothic fortress built by Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV, set dramatically on a forested hillside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Enjoy a private Czech beer culture experience – a curated tasting tour of Prague's finest craft breweries and historic beer halls, including a behind-the-scenes brewery tour. Czech beer is UNESCO-recognized as part of cultural heritage. Optional: premium spa afternoon at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Prague dinner at Field Restaurant (one of Prague's most acclaimed contemporary restaurants) – innovative seasonal tasting menu. Afterward, a private evening river cruise on the Vltava aboard a chartered boat with Champagne, live jazz, and illuminated views of Charles Bridge and Prague Castle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – smoked salmon bagels, avocado toast, fresh-pressed juices, premium loose-leaf teas.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed at Karlštejn Castle grounds – artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, charcuterie, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Field Restaurant – 8-course contemporary Czech seasonal cuisine; followed by Champagne and canapés aboard the private Vltava evening cruise.

day_by_day.notes: Private car to Karlštejn is recommended (30-40 min drive). Book the private Vltava cruise at least 2 weeks in advance. Pack a light jacket for the evening river cruise – September evenings can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Prague hotel after a leisurely breakfast. Private luxury transfer (or first-class train aboard RegioJet Gold or Railjet) departs for Budapest – approximately 6.5–7 hours by scenic train through Central European countryside, or 4 hours by private chauffeur-driven car. Enjoy the journey with curated snacks and beverages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest early-to-mid afternoon. Private luxury transfer to your hotel. Check in and freshen up. Begin with a private panoramic orientation drive of Budapest with your expert local guide – crossing the iconic Chain Bridge, viewing the Parliament Building from the Danube embankment, and getting your bearings of both Buda and Pest sides.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Downtown or Onyx Restaurant (both Michelin-starred) – Hungarian haute cuisine with exceptional wine pairings featuring Tokaj and Egri Bikavér wines. After dinner, a stroll along the illuminated Danube promenade – Budapest truly glows at night.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague hotel breakfast – continental spread with Hungarian-inspired touches (rétes pastry, cold cuts, fresh fruit).
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic or first-class dining car on the train – charcuterie, premium sandwiches, local wines, and mineral water prepared by the hotel.
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner at Onyx Restaurant on Vörösmarty Square – contemporary Hungarian tasting menu (8 courses) with Tokaj wine pairing; stunning Art Nouveau interiors.

day_by_day.notes: First-class train (RegioJet Gold or Austrian Railjet) offers business-class comfort with meals and drinks included – a scenic and relaxing way to travel between cities. Alternatively, a private car offers more flexibility. Book train seats or car well in advance for weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle District (Castle Hill) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church with its stunning geometric roof tiles, and the Fisherman's Bastion offering breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge on foot for the quintessential Budapest photo. Explore the grand Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées) – a UNESCO boulevard lined with neo-Renaissance mansions. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a private guided interior tour. Browse luxury boutiques and art galleries along the avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive thermal spa experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath – arrange a private after-hours or VIP access session (the largest medicinal bath in Europe, housed in a magnificent Neo-Baroque palace). Afterward, dinner at Stand Restaurant (Michelin-starred) – modern Hungarian cuisine celebrating local ingredients and traditions.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast – Hungarian lángos (gourmet version), fresh pastries, cold cuts, cheeses, eggs to order, freshly squeezed juice.
meals.lunch: Elegant Sunday lunch at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square – Budapest's most iconic historic coffeehouse since 1858; traditional Hungarian cakes, Dobos torte, and light savory dishes.
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner at Stand Restaurant – contemporary Hungarian tasting menu; signature dishes include foie gras with Tokaj jelly and Mangalica pork; exceptional Hungarian wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is most magical in the early morning light before crowds arrive. Book VIP/private Széchenyi Spa access in advance – regular public hours can be crowded on weekends. Bring a swimsuit for the thermal experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of Europe's oldest and most beautiful legislative buildings, featuring Gothic Revival architecture, the Hungarian Crown Jewels, and the Holy Crown of Hungary. Exclusive VIP access with a private guide. Afterward, visit St. Stephen's Basilica and ascend to the dome for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) – Budapest's largest and most vibrant indoor market. Shop for premium Hungarian specialties: Tokaj wines, Mangalica salami, hand-painted porcelain (Herend or Zsolnay), paprika, and Hungarian embroidery as luxury souvenirs. Followed by a private guided tour of the historic Jewish Quarter and the magnificent Dohány Street Synagogue – the largest synagogue in Europe.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset private Danube river cruise aboard a chartered luxury boat – sail past the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill as Budapest transforms into a city of golden light. Champagne and canapés on deck. Conclude the evening with dinner at Costes Restaurant (Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant) – innovative contemporary European cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – smoked salmon, Hungarian cold cuts, artisan cheeses, freshly baked kifli rolls, premium coffee and teas.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Michelin-starred) – Hungarian wine-focused cuisine; exceptional wine list with over 200 Hungarian labels; seasonal tasting plates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Restaurant – 6-course contemporary tasting menu; Portuguese-Hungarian fusion influences; world-class wine cellar with sommelier guidance.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours require advance booking – private tours fill up quickly. The Danube cruise is most spectacular starting 30 minutes before sunset (around 18:45 in September). Dress warmly for the open-deck cruise. Dohány Synagogue is closed on Saturdays – Monday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning – sleep in or enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Optional: a peaceful morning walk through Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) – a tranquil green oasis in the middle of the Danube with rose gardens, medieval ruins, and fountains. Alternatively, a final spa treatment at the hotel wellness center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Váci Street or the upscale Deák Ferenc Street area – pick up Herend porcelain, Tokaj Aszú wine, Hungarian leather goods, or bespoke tailoring. Visit the elegant Alexandra Bookstore inside the Párisi Nagy Áruház (Paris Department Store) – a breathtaking Neo-Baroque interior that is a cultural landmark in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at a private dining room or chef's table experience at your hotel restaurant or at Arany Kaviár (Golden Caviar) – Budapest's legendary caviar and fine dining institution specializing in Russian-Hungarian imperial cuisine; beluga caviar, foie gras, and Tokaj Aszú wine. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel – full spread with Hungarian and continental options; freshly baked pastries, smoked meats, cheeses, eggs, fresh fruit, premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch at Café Gerbeaud or New York Café (one of the world's most beautiful cafés) – elegant sandwiches, soups, and legendary Hungarian pastries in a gilded Belle Époque setting.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Arany Kaviár – imperial Russian-Hungarian cuisine; Beluga caviar service, Beef Stroganoff, Blinchiki; paired with vintage Tokaj Aszú 5 Puttonyos for a truly royal send-off.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Budapest airport is approximately 30-40 minutes from the city center by private car. Confirm all luggage weight limits if purchasing premium souvenirs (wines, porcelain). Keep travel documents, hotel folios, and receipts organized for customs if required.
